findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The arithmetic holds: GBP 1300 x 12 = GBP 15,600 a year, and 15,600 / 52 x 5 = GBP 1,500.00. The GBP 1,500 deposit in s6 therefore sits exactly at the five-week cap and does not exceed it. This is a correctly limited amount-cap pass, and it says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. The pass stays conditional because context leaves jurisdiction, tenancy type and rent basis as "unknown". The contract also does not state that the property is in England or that this is an ordinary covered tenancy. Nothing quoted defeats the calculation, so dismissal is not warranted. The issue is not a breach: the amount is compliant, subject to confirming scope and that the rent and deposit relate to the same tenancy. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants

questions: Is this a private tenancy in England with the landlord living elsewhere?
What rent period and tenancy does the deposit cover, and can the amount be revised?

crosscheck.summary: The tenancy agreement names Mira Vale as your landlord, with a representative from a letting agency. But in your messages the agent says the owner is only selling and doesn't know about a tenancy, and that they would issue one in the owner's name anyway. These can't both be true. Ask the agent to confirm in writing who the owner is, and whether the owner has agreed to this letting.
